This French Tiny House Is Perfectly Dreamy, Has the Best Built-in Porch
32 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
Anyone who thinks that the perfect tiny house doesn’t exist should take a closer look at this charming creation from an experienced builder in Occitania, France. A thoughtful layout makes it more spacious than the average mobile home in France, and that’s coupled with beautiful custom features, including a built-in porch, that elevate both beauty and comfort. Lastly, sustainable capabilities add to this home’s eco-friendly quality.
“Camarguaise” could be roughly translated as “the one from Camargue”, a beautiful river delta and coastal region in southern France. This is the name of one of the most impressive custom-builds by Mon Reve en Bois, an artisanal tiny house construction company located in Occitania (another French region famous for its idyllic landscapes).
Tiny house Camarguaise draws attentions immediately with its rounded roof extension, inspired by old gypsy wagons, and the built-in covered porch that brings to mind traditional family homes in the countryside. These two elements are enough to distinguish tiny house Camarguaise from any other French tiny house, but its size also makes an important difference.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois While typical mobile homes in France don’t go past six meters in length (just under 20 feet), Camarguaise boasts a generous 7.3-meter (24 feet). Coupled with a 4-meter (13 feet), this allows for a flexible configuration with a ground-floor bedroom and a loft bedroom. Up to six people can be comfortably accommodated here, and amenities include a lovely dining setup with four seats. This is rare for a French tiny house made entirely of wood, and a great advantage.
Without a doubt, this tiny home’s built-in porch takes the spotlight. First of all, it’s big enough to actually be enjoyed as an outdoor living space, the perfect spot for the morning coffee or simply for watching the sunset. It’s also covered, which adds protection against the elements. Best of all, it’s beautifully crafted, including details such as the slatted fence on both sides, the thin pillars connecting the fence to the roof, and the wavy ornaments.
The rounded, wagon-inspired roof is the final detail that makes this porch extra charming, while the timber itself is the foundation, both literally and figuratively, of this lovely alternative to a conventional exterior deck. The fact that it’s built-in adds the advantage of less hassle, and truth be told, having a tiny home that can travel with its own porch is a great luxury in itself.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Even if this stunning porch was the Camarguaise’s only top selling point, it would be enough, but there’s more. From the porch, guests step right into the kitchen. The ground-floor has a wagon-like layout with the kitchen and dining area on each side, and a central corridor leading to the ground-floor bedroom.
This bedroom is unusual, compared to the typical ground-floor bedrooms you may have seen in other tiny homes. It comes in the form of an intimate nook or recess, which makes it much more bohemian and cozy than a plain bed sitting directly on the floor. The nook walls add privacy without isolating the room entirely. The nook itself also becomes a raised platform for the bed, with extra room for the bespoke corner shelves that act as romantic nightstands.
A big window right by the bed adds the luxury of superb views, while also filling this entire little recess with natural light. The ambiance is cozy and welcoming, and that extra bit of privacy is what makes this bedroom unique and dreamy.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Built-in closets that look almost invisible because they blend so well with the overall cabinetry add functionality to this area of the house. Everything here is custom-built, from the traditional kitchen cupboards to the bedroom closets and the staircase. This staircase deserves extra attention, as it showcases the same kind of woodwork mastery and clever craftsmanship as the built-in porch.
The quarter-turn or L-shaped design of this timber staircase is already unusual, especially for a tiny house, but surprisingly efficient in terms of saving space. It’s far more compact than other types of designs, yet multi-functional. All of the lower treads hide built-in drawers for storage, while the entire outer section, from floor to the loft landing, serves as a spacious pantry with wide, open shelves. All of this is achieved within a miniscule footprint.
The kitchen is typical for French tiny homes, boasting a relatively small countertop, but sufficient storage space for the basics and all the essential appliances (including a small fridge that fits under the counter). There was enough space on the other side for extra cupboards and a second countertop, but the builder chose a more practical alternative, namely a modern-style foldable breakfast bar.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The best part about this breakfast bar is the clever location, which allows room for up to four seats – an impressive number for a French tiny house. It’s also excellent that the bar is entirely foldable, which means that the entire area can be freed to make room for something else without much hassle. Lastly, with large windows both on this side and the kitchen side, this entire part of the house is filled with natural light and surrounded by nature views.
A fully-equipped bathroom completes this home’s functional layout, perfect for full-time accommodation and welcoming enough even for families. The enclosed shower cabin, the sink, and the vanity are part of the standard formula of a conventional bathroom, but the timber paneling throughout is one of the trademarks of artisanal French tiny homes – a mix of traditional and modern features that defines Tiny Camarguaise.
The loft bedroom, easily accessed via the quarter-turn staircase, flaunts a beautiful solid oak floor and large windows. It’s big enough for either a classic double bed or two single beds for young children, which adds to the flexibility of a layout with both a ground-floor bedroom option and a loft.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Described by its builder as a unique and bohemian mix between a tiny house and a wagon, for those who can’t decide between the two, Tiny Camarguaise offers the advantage of a tiny house layout with a loft and the dreamy charm of a gypsy wagon with a built-in porch. And that’s not all. A complete solar power kit makes it self-sufficient in terms of energy.
Adding to its eco-friendly and sustainable nature, Tiny Camarguaise also showcases the beauty and natural strength of locally-sourced timber. Its exterior cladding is made entirely of Douglas fir sourced locally from Occitania forests that are managed sustainably.
This specific type of wood has a high resinous content that makes it particularly resistant to insects and weather damage, as well as naturally water-repellant. An added layer of eco-friendly treatment makes this natural cladding even more durable, as well as low-maintenance.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Everything about Tiny Camarguaise speaks of natural living on multiple levels, from its choice of natural materials to the beautiful porch that invites its owners to spend more time outdoors. Boasting 37 square meters (just under 400 square feet) of floor space, and large windows throughout, this spacious house on wheels offers much more than the average French tiny home, without losing its uniqueness.
The fully-equipped, custom version of Tiny Camarguaise pictured in the gallery was delivered at a price of €58,516 ($65,250) – a great price, considering that it includes the off-grid kit as well, plus all the amenities and appliances. All in all, Tiny Camarguaise has all the qualities of a dream house, including a small price tag.
